high.title: Bursa ends higher on broad-based buying
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 8.43 points at 1,722.19, driven by foreign fund inflows and selective buying in financial, plantation, and industrial sectors. Investor sentiment was boosted by expectations that Malaysia's Q2 GDP will exceed 4%, with results due the following day. Wall Street gains and signs of potential Fed easing further supported the positive momentum.

high.title: Ringgit firms as US rate hike expectations recede
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0710/4.0745 against the US dollar as softer US CPI and PPI data reduced expectations of a Fed rate hike. Fed Chair's remarks to the Senate Banking Committee signalled no urgency to raise rates, benefiting Asian and emerging market currencies. However, the ringgit traded mostly lower against other major currencies.

high.title: Ringgit rises as soft US data weighs on greenback
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0655/4.0710 against the greenback early in the session after US PPI unexpectedly fell 0.3% month-on-month in June, pushing the US Dollar Index down 0.43%. Lower energy prices following the US-Iran ceasefire were a key driver of easing inflation. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's testimony reinforced expectations that rate hikes are not imminent, supporting emerging market currencies including the ringgit.

high.title: Bursa ends lower, weighed by profit-taking in banking, energy stocks
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed down 6.18 points at 1,713.76, dragged by profit-taking in banking and energy sectors amid geopolitical uncertainty. Market breadth remained constructive with healthcare, consumer and plantation stocks outperforming, signalling a defensive rotation. Investors should monitor sector shifts as heightened global risks continue to influence trading sentiment.

high.title: Ringgit ends flat against US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit closed flat at 4.0760/4.0805 against the USD, as markets shifted focus to China's slowing Q2 GDP growth of 4.3%, down from 5% in Q1 2026. A fragile Middle East ceasefire and Trump's threats against Iran over Strait of Hormuz tensions added further pressure. These dual headwinds — China slowdown and geopolitical risk — are critical for Malaysian trade and currency stability.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher ahead of Q2 GDP estimate
high.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0740/4.0780, buoyed by weaker-than-expected US inflation data reducing Fed rate hike fears. Malaysia's Q2 advance GDP figures are due Friday, with Bank Muamalat forecasting 5.1% growth driven by E&E and commodity exports. This GDP release is a key market-moving event for investors assessing Malaysia's economic trajectory.

high.title: Energy, Banking Stocks Lift Bursa
high.summary: The FBM KLCI surged 21.50 points (1.26%) to close at 1,719.94, driven by energy and banking stocks amid escalating US-Iran tensions and fears of oil supply disruptions. Bursa Malaysia outperformed regional peers due to its defensive sector composition and strength in commodity-linked stocks. This represents a significant single-day rally with broad implications for Malaysian equity investors.

high.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar Amid Uncertainties in Middle East
high.summary: Crude oil prices surged sharply with Brent at US$83.12/barrel and WTI at US$78.14/barrel following Trump's declared blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, driving US Treasury yields higher and strengthening the US dollar index to 101.276. The Fed is now expected to potentially raise rates this year, increasing pressure on emerging market currencies including the ringgit. Analysts forecast the ringgit-dollar to trade in a volatile range of 4.07–4.10.

high.title: Ringgit Ends Lower Against US Dollar Amid Cautious Sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0760/4.0800 against the US dollar by end of day as markets awaited the US June CPI data, with headline inflation expected at 3.8% year-on-year. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and potential Strait of Hormuz disruptions risk renewed inflationary pressures, keeping risk appetite guarded. This currency weakness has direct implications for Malaysian import costs and monetary policy outlook.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds on stronger investor appetite
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.30 points to 1,718.06 at the morning open, supported by improved global risk sentiment following softer US producer inflation data. Technology counters were highlighted as likely beneficiaries of selective buying interest. The broader market saw losers outnumber gainers early in the session, suggesting cautious but improving sentiment.

medium.title: US retail sales lose steam in June as consumers spend less on gasoline
medium.summary: US retail sales grew only 0.2% month-on-month in June, a sharp deceleration from May's 1.0% jump, as gasoline station sales tumbled 5.3% on lower energy costs. Excluding motor vehicles and parts, sales declined 0.2%, signalling softer US consumer demand. This data is relevant to Malaysian exporters and investors tracking US economic health and its implications for global trade.

medium.title: Bursa gains on improved sentiment ahead of GDP data
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.15 points in early trade, lifted by Wall Street's semiconductor rebound and softer US June inflation data that eased rate hike concerns. The US 10-year Treasury yield dipped to 4.587%, providing a positive backdrop for emerging market equities including Malaysia. This early session optimism set the stage for intraday dynamics ahead of Friday's GDP release.

medium.title: Syahrul Azmir made new CEO of Rapid Bus
medium.summary: Rapid Bus appointed Syahrul Azmir as its new CEO, bringing over 27 years of logistics, supply chain and transport experience. The appointment aligns with Rapid Bus's push to expand electric bus deployment and improve service reliability across Rapid KL and Rapid Penang networks. This leadership change is relevant to investors tracking Malaysia's public transportation and EV transition sector.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Higher on Healthcare, Property Buying
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened modestly higher at 1,700.85 amid early buying in healthcare and property sectors, though market breadth was negative with decliners outnumbering gainers. Wall Street fell overnight as US-Iran tensions escalated and Trump declared a Strait of Hormuz blockade, causing Brent crude to spike to US$83/barrel. This opening snapshot provides early context for the day's significant market movements.

medium.title: Ringgit Closes Higher Against Major Regional Currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit edged up to 4.0680/4.0730 against the US dollar on Monday as investors assessed uncertainties around the US-Iran ceasefire and Strait of Hormuz vessel traffic. Crude oil remained elevated with WTI at US$73.02 and Brent at US$77.80 per barrel, while US rate futures pointed to a 55.7% probability of a September rate hike. The strengthening US dollar outlook continues to pose headwinds for the ringgit.

medium.title: Plantation, commodity stocks lift Bursa higher at close
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 6.95 points (0.41%) at 1,698.44, briefly breaching the key 1,700-level during late afternoon trading. Plantation and commodity stocks were the main drivers of the gain, with turnover improving to 3.09 billion units worth RM2.23 billion. Rakuten Trade's equity research head remains cautiously optimistic despite elevated geopolitical risks.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher before slipping on profit-taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 1.81 points higher at 1,693.30 before slipping 2.49 points to 1,689.0 due to early profit-taking activity. Market breadth was negative with decliners outnumbering gainers, reflecting cautious sentiment at the open. The positive lead from Wall Street, driven by tech stocks, provided initial support but failed to sustain early gains.
